subject: Day 65: textured-toy exploration
bodyText:
Today's focus
At week 10, Avi brings his hands to his mouth on purpose and inspects them with interest. This week is built for hands-and-mouth sensory play: give him varied surfaces to mouth and narrate what he is feeling.

Action items
- Assemble a rotating tray of three safe textured objects today: a silicone teether, a soft fabric book, and a smooth wooden ring. Avoid anything with small loose parts, which remain a choking hazard at this age. AAP HealthyChildren: baby ages and stages: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Keep cumulative tummy time at 60-plus minutes per day, staggered into four to six short bouts; he should be pushing up on his forearms with his chest off the floor. AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Continue logging feeds and outputs in whatever app you use; you will want a clean record on hand if any fever workup comes up before day 90.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Profuse drooling and constant hand-sucking. This reflects salivary-gland maturation, not necessarily teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6 to 10 months.
- [monitor] Persistent head asymmetry or a favored head-turn to one side (positional plagiocephaly or torticollis). Vary which shoulder you hold him against and raise it at the next visit if it is not resolving.
- [call within 24h] Decreased feeding lasting 24 hours or more, or any new color change during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, an apnea episode, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 for blue lips and do not wait!

Enrichment opportunities
- Offer the silicone teether, fabric book, and wooden ring one at a time and let him mouth and grip each; varied surfaces build the tactile map his fingers will rely on later. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Let him bring his hands to his mouth and study them during floor time; this self-exploration is the cognitive front edge of the hand-eye coordination that tummy time keeps reinforcing. AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Narrate each texture as he mouths it (soft, bumpy, smooth, cool); pairing words to sensation feeds the serve-and-return loop linked to stronger later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): low-grade fussiness, drowsiness, or mild fever after the 2-month shots should be fully past by now; a new fever is treated as non-vaccine and warrants a same-day call.
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; start firming up a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
